title: A closer look at IC 5201
caption: The barred spiral galaxy IC 5201, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: IC 5201, LEDA 27893 · constellation Grus · about 40 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows the barred spiral galaxy IC 5201 in the southern constellation of Grus, the Crane. Like about two thirds of the spiral galaxies in the Universe, our Milky Way included, it has a bar of stars cutting through its centre.

The galaxy was first spotted in 1900 by Joseph Lunt, a British–South African astronomer looking through a telescope at Cape Town Observatory. More than a century later, astronomers are still interested in it.

To make this image, Hubble used its Advanced Camera for Surveys, which can pick out individual stars in other galaxies. That ability makes it a powerful tool for tracing how different populations of stars were born, evolved and died across the cosmos. IC 5201 itself lies more than 40 million light-years away from us.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.27 x 3.38 arcminutes) and distance (40 million light years), the frame spans roughly 38,000 × 39,000 light-years. Its light set out about 40 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using filters at 606 and 814 nm, in visible and near-infrared light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and resolving single stars in a galaxy this far away is only possible with a telescope like Hubble.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: A galactic bar is a long, straight concentration of stars across a spiral galaxy's centre, from which the spiral arms often seem to unwind. Bars are common enough that they are a normal feature of spiral galaxies rather than an oddity.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with a bar of stars across its centre.
